A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Robust Federated Inference. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. Retained content can be matched despite appendix renumbering and inserted material.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and AG-News, including attack comparisons, scalability tests, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds mixed-attack evaluations and measurements of inference latency and training time.

M1.justification: DeepSet-TM's architecture, training objective, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The auxiliary logit-space SIA rule has a small boundary change: v1 uses the maximum logit when it equals zero, whereas v3 substitutes the negated minimum (Appendices D.3/F.3). This changes possible attack outputs without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The three datasets and classification tasks are retained. Appendix G.2.3 adds a heterogeneous-adversary scenario in which four clients simultaneously apply different existing attacks, extending evaluation beyond a shared attack type.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Mean, CWMed, CWTM, GM, COPUR, manifold projection, and the randomized-ablation variants. The new mixed-attack and timing studies reuse existing methods; no comparison method is introduced or removed.

E3.justification: V3 adds latency measurement in milliseconds per 64-sample batch, averaged across the test set, and wall-clock comparisons of ordinary and adversarial training. The mixed-attack protocol uses n = 17, f = 4, and alpha = 0.5. Existing data splits and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G.2.3 newly tests robustness when adversaries use different attack types simultaneously. Appendix G.8 adds computational-overhead analyses. Existing component ablations, heterogeneity studies, scalability tests, and increased-PGD-compute analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and reporting means with standard deviations. V3 continues this reporting practice and averages training times over five runs; it introduces no increased run count, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Retained accuracy tables and plotted results are unchanged. New Table 8 reports mixed-attack DeepSet-TM accuracies of 63.7%, 74.9%, and 83.9% on the three datasets. Table 14 adds latency results, and Appendix G.8.2 reports adversarial training taking 86–100 minutes versus roughly 1–3 minutes without it.

T1.justification: V3 adds Theorem 2, a Lipschitz-based robustness-gap bound for nonlinear DeepSet, its Appendix C proof, and an Appendix D derivation comparing aggregation without robust averaging. It also restores the missing averaging normalization and corrects the Section 3 counterexample. These substantially extend the formal analysis beyond v1's averaging guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: formalizing robust federated inference, analyzing robust averaging, and combining adversarially trained DeepSet with test-time robust aggregation. The headline 4.7–22.2 percentage-point improvement claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning nonlinear sensitivity, removal of corruption-magnitude dependence through CWTM, and generalization to heterogeneous adversaries. It also argues that the newly quantified training and inference costs are acceptable for cross-silo use. Earlier interpretations are largely retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds a repository link and a statement announcing release of the complete codebase, together with timing measurements and their measurement details. The existing implementation and hyperparameter descriptions are retained in renamed Appendix F.

R1.justification: The bibliography and dedicated related-work discussions are retained. New Appendix G.2.3 adds limited positioning of the mixed-attack experiment against the coordinated attacks commonly considered in Byzantine-learning literature, using existing references.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. V3 makes localized grammatical and notation edits, rewrites the logit-space SIA explanation, renumbers appendices around new material, and adds acknowledgments, a reproducibility statement, and an LLM-usage statement.

P2.justification: V3 adds the mixed-attack and latency tables, relocates retained displays, and updates captions and cross-references. The four figure graphics and existing table designs are retained. Conference headers and local page reflow do not constitute a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful mixed-attack evidence, timing transparency, code-access information, and mathematical corrections. However, its new nonlinear guarantee has an unresolved proof gap: between Equations (19) and (20), Appendix C bounds transformed-coordinate variation using the same input coordinate, although Section 4 assumes Lipschitz continuity with respect to the full Euclidean input norm. The empirical and reproducibility benefits coexist with uncertainty about this substantial new theoretical contribution, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
